correctness.rationale: Taylor expansion in powers δ yields column moment vectors u_r and row node monomials v_r. The leading second exterior-power norm is δ sqrt(µ2) sqrt(6+2t²), while the third is δ³(1-t²)sqrt(µ2 Δ): the 1/2 quadratic Taylor factor cancels the Vandermonde determinant 2(1-t²). Largest singular value tends sqrt3, so the ratio gives the exact smallest-singular-value coefficient. Reflection symmetry removes odd moments, µ2>0 and Δ>0 avoid rank loss. For t>0, d(log f)/dt=-2t/(1-t²)-2t/(6+2t²)<0, giving unique midpoint. Independently constructed high-precision Fourier Gram matrices at t=0,.5 and δ=0.002 agreed to about 1e-7 relative error. This checks examples, not the asymptotic universal proof.

final_claim: For a fixed finite reflection-symmetric positively weighted Fourier aperture with Δ=µ4-µ2²>0, the three-source cluster x=(-1,t,1) has σ_min(Aδ(t))/δ²→sqrt(Δ)(1-t²)/sqrt(6+2t²), uniquely maximized at midpoint t=0; the sharp leading condition number there is 3sqrt(2)/sqrt(Δ).
limitations: Fixed positive symmetric aperture, Δ>0, fixed t ∈(-1,1); no joint bandwidth/separation scaling.
